entities.name: ueno bank S.A.
entities.desc: Paraguayan digital bank (ex-Financiera El Comercio → Financiera Ueno → bank Nov 2023; absorbed Visión Banco 2024). ~9% of system, ~2.9–3M customers. In resolution under BCP since 2–3 Nov 2026.
entities.status: In resolution (Ley 2334/03 art. 13 b); interveners appointed

entities.name: Grupo Vázquez S.A.E.
entities.desc: Controlling conglomerate (~23 companies: finance, tech, retail, cattle). Chaired by F. Miguel Vázquez Villasanti.
entities.status: Under criminal investigation (causa 89/2026); assets seized; bankruptcy petition filed 11 Nov — not declared; 22 firms shut since 3 Nov (MTESS: 3,610 PY workers unpaid); Mensaje 432 lacks votes per Senate president (23 Nov); Executive bill (25 Nov) advances up to 5 minimum wages to >4,000 workers of ~40 linked firms (fund G. 62,000M); workers' advance bill postponed in the Senate to the following week (26 Nov); ex-workers march again for 100% severance

entities.name: U Holdings S.à r.l. (Luxembourg)
entities.desc: Holding created 29 Sep 2023 (RCS B280698); sole shareholder of U Paraguay S.A.; Grupo Vázquez 86.73% capital/98.82% votes; OTP Bank 9.99%.

entities.name: U Paraguay S.A.
entities.desc: Holds 93.05% of ueno bank.
entities.status: ; general inhibition + account freeze (39-company order, 24 Nov)

entities.name: Ueno Holding S.A.E.C.A.
entities.desc: Holding (ex-Credicentro lineage) incl. Ueno Seguros, itti; Peña held 6,144 shares (declared 2023), sold by Mar 2025.
entities.status: ; general inhibition + account freeze (39-company order, 24 Nov)

entities.name: Ueno AFPISA
entities.desc: Fund manager (Ueno Cash Guaraníes / Dólares mutual funds; ~30,000 investors, ~US$46M).
entities.status: Authorization suspended 180 days by Superintendencia de Valores (res. 10 Nov 2026); lost capacity to operate per BCP/SIV; fund securities in Cavapy custody; alternatives under evaluation (BCP, 24 Nov); e-mailing unitholders (units at 6 Nov) on full redemption; no dates/values (24 Nov); BCP: AFPISA must design the payment plan; investors told funds head to liquidation (no administrator accepted) vs CAVAPY: transfer within ~2 weeks (25 Nov); 25 Nov: SIV temporarily lifted its suspension — weekly redemptions up to G. 30M via Investor Casa de Bolsa (paying agent) from next week; unit-holders' assembly to decide on liquidation; 26 Nov BCP conference: second weekly G. 30M window (up to G. 60M in two weeks, ~98–99% of ~30,000 unit-holders); Investor to sell CDAs/bonds at par; assembly date still pending

entities.name: Vinanzas S.A.
entities.desc: Related company; alleged simulated purchase of ueno's impaired portfolio (16 Jun 2026, US$74.4M).
entities.status: Named in imputations; second raid 26 Nov; 15-day closure requested so BCP technicians can review documents; prosecutors cite a US$75M portfolio (vs US$74.4M earlier)

entities.name: Red Digital S.A. / Red Digital de Procesamiento S.A.
entities.desc: Related firms receiving G. 876,700M irrevocable contributions (39.7% of effective equity, per ABC).

entities.name: itti S.A.E.
entities.desc: Group tech company; bonds allegedly bought by Technoma/Factopar.

entities.name: OTP Bank Plc
entities.desc: Hungarian bank; 9.99% of U Holdings (~US$30M, 2025–26).

entities.name: Banco Central del Paraguay (BCP)
entities.desc: Regulator/resolution authority. Board now: Jorge Schreiner (pres.), Fernando Rivarola, Pedro Acosta, plus others per reports.
entities.status: ; 26 Nov: no new FGD payouts planned (USD 644M already used, ~USD 900M remains); exclusion balance expected 30 Nov

entities.name: Superintendencia de Bancos (BCP)
entities.desc: Banking supervisor; head Holger Insfrán (Apr 2024–Nov 2026).

entities.name: Fondo de Garantía de Depósitos (FGD)
entities.desc: Deposit guarantee: 75 minimum wages (G. 228.3M) per depositor; Ley 7745 advance up to 40 wages (G. 121.76M). Director José Maciel.

entities.name: Instituto de Previsión Social (IPS)
entities.desc: Main social security/pension fund; ~US$516.4M exposed per its own filing.
entities.status: Offices raided 19 Nov 2026 (2,000–3,000 documents seized per its legal director); no IPS officials charged; legal director changed 12–13 Nov (Morínigo → Galeano)

entities.name: Municipalidad de Asunción
entities.desc: Capital city government. Mayors: Óscar 'Nenecho' Rodríguez (to Aug 2025), Luis Bello (2025–Nov 2026), Soledad Núñez (from early Nov 2026).
entities.status: Complainant (13 Nov); T1 balance at 31 Oct: three ueno accounts ~G. 1,793M (adviser now says G. 1,900M retained); liabilities ~G. 2.4 tn; Catastro review finds 2020 file naming Miguel Vázquez as 'social occupant'; corte administrativo signing date disputed (20 vs 24 Nov)

entities.name: Ministerio Público (Fiscalía)
entities.desc: Prosecution service; Unidad Especializada de Delitos Económicos y Anticorrupción.

entities.name: Congreso Nacional
entities.desc: Impeached Peña (5–6 Nov); bicameral inquiry commission approved by Senate 18 Nov, pending in Diputados.

entities.name: Asociación de Bancos del Paraguay (Asoban)
entities.desc: Banking association; formal note to Peña & BCP (Sept 2026) on related-party exposure; earlier note 18 Jun 2025.

entities.name: Itaipú Binacional
entities.desc: ~US$163.8M + G. 115,200M in ueno (3 Nov 2026). Brazilian side asked (20 Nov) to re-evaluate banks authorised for Itaipú funds. Awarded Dobrestec (GSR Security) surveillance contracts NE 0504-26 for G. 32,746M in two lots (ABC 22 Nov).
entities.status: Complainant (7 Nov); board member N. Duarte Frutos: placements in ueno >US$200M (24 Nov, conflicts with US$163.8–182M); DG Zárate: ~US$228M incl. PTI (25 Nov, conflicts with earlier figures); FM Ramírez Lezcano pledges to Brazil to restitute Itaipú funds (25 Nov); board members Duarte Frutos/Riquelme: US$220–222M incl. PTI, all Paraguayan side (25 Nov); 26 Nov: Ramírez repeats restitution pledge to Brazil (no method); Zárate itemises ~US$163–163.8M + G. 115,000–115,200M + PTI ~US$40M ≈ US$220M and says Itaipú filed a criminal complaint over retained funds

entities.name: CONMEBOL
entities.desc: South American football confederation; reportedly US$14M trapped in ueno.

entities.name: SEPRELAD
entities.desc: Anti-money-laundering secretariat (Liliana Alcaraz).
entities.status: Under public criticism (ABC, CADEP, Sen. Paredes, 18–22 Nov); no proceedings against its head found; Dep. Raúl Benítez draft resolution urging Alliana to remove minister Liliana Alcaraz (to be moved 24 Nov); SEPRELAD note (9 Nov) disclaims bank-supervision powers; absent from 23 Nov FGE coordination meeting; Diputados to consider Benítez's removal draft on 24 Nov (outcome pending); removal draft not studied — Diputados session lost quorum (24 Nov); Seprelad tells UDEA supervision is the SB's job; Sen. Mario Varela (ANR) and ex-Sen. Querey demand minister Alcaraz's resignation/removal (25 Nov)

entities.name: Banco Atlas / Grupo Zuccolillo
entities.desc: Zuccolillo family bank (and ABC Color owner per El Parámetro). No ownership link to ueno found.

entities.name: Grupo Cartes / Banco Basa
entities.desc: Horacio Cartes' group; prior business links (2019 bond with Credicentro).

entities.name: Santiago Peña Palacios
entities.desc: Former President of Paraguay (15 Aug 2023 – 6 Nov 2026). Ex-shareholder of Ueno Holding until Mar 2025.
entities.status: Impeached 6 Nov; imputed (causa 92/2026: lesión de confianza, administración en provecho propio; + asociación criminal 13 Nov); prisión preventiva — Regimiento Escolta Presidencial 6–16 Nov, Viñas Cué military prison since 16 Nov; phone-data extraction authorised; defence complains (21 Nov) of only 4 h/day outside cell; judge Legal's competence upheld (A.I. 420, appeal pending); expelled from ANR; denies wrongdoing; presumed innocent; regime at Viñas Cué eased by court oficio (20 Nov): same hours as other inmates, may socialise with unrelated inmates; AC/fridge request under study (23 Nov); filed acción de inconstitucionalidad vs Senate Res. N.º 3 (impeachment) before the CSJ Sala Constitucional (23 Nov); brother Francisco detained (23 Nov); imputation EXPANDED 24 Nov (Acta N.º 11): + lavado de activos (coautor) and cohecho pasivo agravado (autor); presumed innocent; missed earlier: judge Legal lifted isolation restrictions at Viñas Cué (oficio 20–21 Nov; NPY 23 Nov); still in prisión preventiva; presumed innocent

entities.name: Pedro Alliana
entities.desc: Former VP; sworn in as President 6 Nov 2026, term to Aug 2028.
entities.status: President since 6 Nov; no allegations against him found; opposition (Filizzola) and analysts criticise continuity of Peña-era officials (21–22 Nov); announced (24 Nov) bill advancing up to 5 minimum wages (G. 15.22M) per ex-Grupo Vázquez worker, IPS cover to 31 Dec; to meet Milei 25/26 Nov; sworn declaration (26 Nov): ueno CDA G. 1,500M (share; vs G. 4,500M said earlier) and ueno loans balance G. 3,628M; no allegation of wrongdoing

entities.name: Federico Miguel Vázquez Villasanti
entities.desc: Head of Grupo Vázquez; ex-CEO / VP1 of ueno bank (titles vary by outlet).
entities.status: Detained 3 Nov; imputed (causa 89/2026); prisión preventiva (ex-Tacumbú); charges widened 10 Nov (asociación criminal, lavado); prisión preventiva FIRM after defence withdrew appeal (A.I. 372, 26 Nov)

entities.name: Juan Manuel Gustale
entities.desc: President of ueno bank.
entities.status: Prisión preventiva (ex-Tacumbú), confirmed on appeal 10 Nov

entities.name: Julio Daniel Rey Fernández
entities.desc: Ex-VP2 (ABC) / VP (BBC) of ueno bank.
entities.status: Prisión preventiva (ex-Tacumbú); only investigated director who testified — alleged night cash delivery (US$17M + G.17,000M), hidden losses, Pear S.R.L./Francisco Peña deal, Comitia–ITTI payments (20 Nov); presumed innocent; defence denies leaking his statement and seeks security guarantees (23 Nov)

entities.name: Alejandro Gómez Abente
entities.desc: Director (titular), ueno bank.
entities.status: Prisión preventiva (ex-Tacumbú)

claims.statement: 'Delirio colectivo' report: an employee of ueno's liquidity area (identity withheld) warned Rey in Oct 2025 about the real liquidity channels (refunds/reintegros, clearing, card use) and how little money remained; he testified as a witness (19 Nov) and Rey handed the report to prosecutors. Per ÚH, Rey alleges ~US$900M of real expenses (technology, aggressive refund promotions, operations) were disguised as assets/loans receivable via property and software deals with Grupo Vázquez firms (Grupo Hendy, Mowi, Grupo M, TUIU, Franede, Office Design, Henrichi, Model, Data Force). Rey says he investigated until he was dismissed in March 2026. v1.4 (ÚH, 22 Nov, quoting the report): a section 'Extra – ¿Cuánto durarán los bonos internacionales (300M USD) sin gestión?' concluded the international bond money would last ~8 months 'sin gestión' ('El cambio debe ser estructural, no un patch'); 55–70% of daily cash outflows ran through clearing (Mastercard, Infonet, cheques), fintech/collection networks (Netel, Wepa), Tigo and IPS pension payouts. DISCREPANCY (unresolved): ÚH dates the report to Oct 2025 and it speaks of US$300M of international bonds, whereas the issue on record is US$350M in Mar 2026 (C-COL-12) — possibly a planned issue at the time; not clarified by ÚH. UPDATE v1.6 (La Nación, El Observador, 23 Nov, citing the record of Rey's 4 Nov declaración indagatoria): the 'Delirio Colectivo' file (20 pages) was e-mailed on 13 Oct 2025 by Lucca de Barba of the Liquidity area to Mariana Torres and Rey, noting the matter had been discussed with Miguel Vázquez; the ~US$900M breaks down roughly into US$300M of refunds (reintegros), US$300M of technology spending and other items; between Oct 2025 and Mar 2026, when the BCP became restrictive, the asset-swap scheme turned into loans to linked and non-linked firms. NAMING DIFFERENCE: ÚH withheld the employee's identity; La Nación/El Observador name Lucca de Barba (already an entity in this dossier). UPDATE v1.8 (ABC, 24 Nov, document given to ABC by ueno staff and in prosecutors' hands): the 20-page file is dated September 2025 (e-mailed 13 Oct 2025 — date conflict Sep vs Oct recorded, likely drafting vs sending); it said liquid securities were 'apalancados al 100% diario', institutional-deposit concentration rose from 16% to 31%, the bank breached VaR1, liquidity-buffer, acid and forced-liquidity ratios, ran a daily oversold FX position, froze disbursements and paid suppliers late; a 14-month cash projection (Aug 2025–Sep 2026) was negative every month and a section estimated how long the US$300M international bonds would last 'sin gestión' (~8 months). ABC notes De Barba also worked from tech firm Itti.

claims.statement: Rey also told prosecutors that 'COMITIA realiza pagos a ITTI' (Grupo Vázquez's tech arm) for the award of the electoral voting-machine lease, and that the quiniela business ran via 'Data Force', also linked to the group (Diana Jara handled tenders). The TSJE (Justicia Electoral) replied it has never had a contractual link with ITTI; Comitia told the TSJE it has no shareholding in Grupo Vázquez and only hired Ueno Seguros for transport insurance. ABC notes Comitia had failed 26 technical tests, was the sole bidder for the lease (awarded Dec 2025), and that the Gross Brown law firm (Eduardo Gross Brown: alternate director of ueno bank) represented the Comitia-MSA consortium. UPDATE v1.6 (23 Nov): TSJE minister Jaime Bestard (ABC Cardinal 730 AM) denied any relationship between the Electoral Justice and Grupo Vázquez and said it never had accounts at ueno; Congress president Basilio 'Bachi' Núñez said 'todo se tiene que explicar… vamos a apoyar a los colegas que soliciten los vínculos' (Ñandutí). RDN recalls ueno approved a US$14M credit line backing the MSA-Comitia bid in the 2025 tender (US$93M estimate). UPDATE v1.7 (23 Nov): Sens. Lilian and Arnaldo Samaniego filed a draft resolution asking the TSJE for documents on the Comitia-MSA contract (5 Dec 2025, US$34,986,500, 18,000 machines); ex-candidate Paraguayo Cubas' defence will ask that Rey testify as a witness in his trial over the 2023 post-election riots (trial postponed). UPDATE v2.3 (ÚH/RDN, 26 Nov): they report that Technoma SAECA, described as Grupo Vázquez-linked, provides the TSJE's data-backup platform (Exagrid requirements in the tender). The articles retrace a 2025 tender path (cancelled US$ 93M machine purchase; later lease of 18,000 machines to Consorcio Comitia–MSA for US$ 35 million) and allege a money flow into Grupo Vázquez/itti bonds that financed the Vinanzas US$ 74.4M portfolio purchase (already in C-COL-06). The TSJE on 20–21 Nov again denied contractual ties with itti. These are press allegations, not charges against TSJE officials. Municipal elections were due 29 Nov 2026.

claims.statement: Executive bill (Mensaje N.º 432, received by the Senate 13 Nov; formal entry 18 Nov session; sent to four committees) would place companies linked to ueno bank — same economic group or declared related by ownership/management, including firms that left the group in the prior 12 months via transfers to insiders/relatives — automatically under an 8-month temporary-administration regime. A Consejo de Supervisión de Sociedades Vinculadas under the MIC (chaired by the Presidency; MIC, MEF, MTESS; BCP with voice but no vote) would identify firms, appoint/remove administrators, authorise asset/unit sales and report possible crimes to prosecutors; non-viable firms can be excluded. MIC minister Marco Riquelme says it costs the State nothing; Senate president Basilio 'Bachi' Núñez backs it (cites 42 firms, ~6,000 jobs) but is open to reviewing the proposed immunity for administrators. NOTE: predates this cycle; missed in v1.0–v1.2. CHANGE v1.6 (23 Nov): Congress/Senate president Basilio 'Bachi' Núñez now says the bill lacks the votes 'como viene del Ejecutivo' and that the 'most healthy' course is to send it to committee 'para que duerma el sueño de los justos' — 'no hay intención… desde la propia bancada colorada' (Ñandutí) — a reversal from his earlier backing (recorded, not resolved). He also said the ueno case is ~7% of the financial system and does not endanger the ANR ahead of 2028 (Ñandutí). Ex-workers' spokespeople again rejected the bill (Hoy, La Tribuna). UPDATE v1.8 (24 Nov): Núñez reiterated at a press conference that there are no Senate votes; the bill would go to committees and could 'dormir el sueño de los justos' unless heavily amended; he points to Sen. Derlis Maidana's Senabico-law amendment as a middle way (El Nacional, Ñandutí). Ex-workers' spokesperson Cheryl Cazuriaga (GEN via La Nación) again rejects reactivation and asks the State to advance severance.

claims.statement: ABC (23 Nov), citing internal Grupo Vázquez documents held by prosecutors, reports that ANR deputy Jatar 'Oso' Fernández (then aligned with Peña) received a ueno bank loan of G. 216.2M on 1 Jul 2025 — a week after he voted in Diputados (24 Jun 2025) for Ley N.º 7503 del Sistema Nacional de Pagos, promulgated by Peña on 27 Jun and criticised as tailored to ueno — and that from August 2025 the bank was instructed to pay him >G. 20M a month for the 60-month life of the loan: G. 15M with no stated justification plus the loan instalment (first transfer G. 20,848,931 on 6 Aug 2025 from the bank's 'Proveedores G.' account; later payments to be withdrawn in cash). Fernández (780 AM/Mega TV) says the payments were sponsorships for his rally racing, 'todo con factura', that his loan (~G. 200M, to 2030) is normal and denies any link to his vote ('no es ilegal tener auspiciante'). UPDATE v1.7 (23 Nov): Fernández publicly acknowledged receiving ~G. 20M a month via a ueno account, calling it rally sponsorship ('no es ilegal que yo tenga un auspiciante'; 'ueno auspiciaba a todo el mundo'), says he will repay the ~G. 200M loan (due 2030) and that it had 'nothing to do' with his votes on the payments and conflict-of-interest laws; Dep. Miguel Martínez (PLRA) called him 'corrupto y vendido'. No prosecutorial action found; presumed innocent. UPDATE v1.9 (SNT, 1000 Noticias, 24 Nov): Fernández says the arrangement was made directly with Miguel Vázquez, the banked money was declared and used to repay a personal G. 200M loan; his rally structure cost ~G. 30M a month.

claims.statement: ÚH exclusive (23 Nov) on the ueno–Visión Banco merger feasibility plan filed with the BCP (expediente EXP-2024-004110): it requested deferring G. 2.68 trillion of Visión's impaired portfolio and creating a G. 2.52 trillion trust for merger expenses/investments — together ~G. 5.2 trillion, ~3.3× the merged bank's projected equity — spread over up to 20 years; a 0% risk weight for the deferred assets in the solvency ratio; suspension of provisioning on certain loans from the merger date; a 20-year deferral of Visión's accumulated 2023 loss (G. 88,984M); postponed provisions on foreclosed assets; projections assumed a US$50M capital injection and a decade of profit capitalisation. ÚH headline: 'Sin beneficios del BCP no hubiera existido'. Consistent with Asoban president Osvaldo Serafini (5Días, 20 Nov): the 'pecado original' was approving the merger with regulatory exceptions that distorted solvency, the second being the later emptying of assets; he also faulted rating agencies and auditors. Which of the requested measures the BCP board actually granted (Rivarola: the approval included bond issuance and 'flexibilidades', C-CB-09) is not itemised in the sources. UPDATE v1.8 (ÚH, RDN 24 Nov, from the BCP file): the joint Superintendencia report SB GAR N.º 043/2024 + SB GS N.º 001/2024 of 16 May 2024 found the feasibility plan economically viable, recommended proceeding and judged the 20-year horizon reasonable — 12 officials signed, most signatures between 16:12 and 17:11 (one more at 09:54 next day); the BCP legal unit found no legal breach; the BCP board authorised continuing on 27 May and approved the absorption on 21 Jun 2024 (signatories of those two resolutions not identifiable in the file). Context: Dec 2023 assets ueno G. 3.1 tn vs Visión G. 8.2 tn (67 branches, >1M clients); Grupo Vázquez then owned 89.85% of ueno (cf. 93.05% U Paraguay stake in C-OWN-01 — different dates/levels, not reconciled); merger commitment 6 Feb 2024, swap 1 ueno share per 10 Visión shares with no supporting valuation in the file; extraordinary assemblies approved unanimously 6 Mar 2024. In Jan 2025 the BCP authorised amending the plan to allow non-subordinated bonds up to US$500M — signed by Humberto Colmán, Carmen Marín Rodríguez, Liana Caballero Krause and Miguel Mora (Caballero Krause, Mora and Marco Aurelio González are now detained). This partly answers the earlier open question on what the board granted; individual concessions actually approved still not itemised.

claims.statement: Labour minister Mónica Recalde (Telefuturo, via La Nación, Hoy, ADN, 23 Nov): 22 Grupo Vázquez companies that worked exclusively for ueno (no own clients; cross-shareholdings) have been shut since 3 Nov with no one administering them — an 'indirect dismissal'; ~5,000 jobs affected: 3,610 workers in Paraguay without work or severance (~40,000 people with families) and ~1,000 in Argentina; ~490 bank employees already received their finiquitos; 52 other group firms keep operating because they have real markets; some salaries reached G. 250M a month. claims.statement: ARREST OF PEÑA'S BROTHER: by Resolución Fiscal N.º 12 of 23 Nov 2026 (causa 92/2026, art. 240 CPP — detention to secure presence for indagatoria), the prosecutors of the Unidad Especializada de Delitos Económicos y Anticorrupción ordered the detention of Francisco Peña Palacios (brother of ex-President Santiago Peña) and his wife Rocío Caballero Bosch, both linked to PEAR S.R.L. The Ministerio Público says the case concerns the purchase of a 1,184-ha rural property in María Antonia (Paraguarí) for ~US$3M through an operation linked to the then Financiera Ueno; its hypothesis is that PEAR was used as the vehicle, that one of the investigated persons controlled the company before formally becoming partner/legal representative, and that the loan instalments were not paid from PEAR's own income but were assumed by Grupo Vázquez-linked companies — invoices of Jun and Aug 2026 for US$739,000 and G. 295,650,000 for 'provisión de granos forrajeros' to the group's estancia Don Miguel are under analysis. Suspected offences: lavado de activos (art. 196 CP) and administración en provecho propio (art. 8 Ley 2523/04). On the afternoon of 23 Nov police (Comisaría 11.ª) intercepted Francisco Peña as he was leaving his home in Los Laureles (Asunción); without a search warrant they waited for his lawyer Elías Gibbons Dávalos, after which he surrendered, was handcuffed and hooded and taken (~18:15 local) to the Departamento contra el Crimen Organizado after a medical check; Rocío Caballero Bosch presented herself at the same department. As of ~02:00 UTC 24 Nov neither had been formally imputed (indagatoria pending). CONFLICTS: the fiscal team is six prosecutors per MP (C. Benítez, S. González, V. Valdez, L. Giacummo, R. Benítez, M. González) vs seven per ABC (adds Elena Fiore); Hoy lists six offences (lesión de confianza, documentos públicos falsos — producción/uso —, asociación criminal, lavado, administración en provecho propio) vs two in the MP release; La República (CO) speaks of a 'detención preventiva' request (not supported by the MP release). Presumed innocent. UPDATE v1.9: superseded by Acta de Imputación N.º 11 (24 Nov) — see C-PEN-32.

claims.statement: Peña files unconstitutionality action against his removal: at 08:20 on 23 Nov his lawyer Ricardo Preda filed an acción de inconstitucionalidad before the Sala Constitucional of the Supreme Court (ministers Gustavo Santander, Víctor Ríos Ojeda, César Diesel) seeking nullity of Senate Resolución N.º 3 of 6 Nov 2026 (impeachment for mal desempeño). He alleges violation of arts. 16 (defence), 17 (due process, incs. 7–9) and 256 of the Constitution: the accusation and a >300-page file were delivered at 22:15 with the hearing at 10:00 the next morning (~12 night hours), a 72-hour extension was refused, and 'illicit' evidence (untraceable recordings, press items, third-party invoices) was used; he rebuts the conflict-of-interest and IPS counts (shares declared and sold; ueno's bank licence a BCP decision; IPS autonomous). Hoy: no precautionary suspension was requested. ABC recalls the Court rejected Fernando Lugo's 2012 action as 'non-justiciable'. Dep. (Roberto/Eduardo — ABC names both) González says it will not prosper. CONFLICT on the Senate vote: ÚH '43 legisladores' vs Hoy '44 votos' (and C-PEN-06: 44–0). UPDATE v1.8 (24 Nov): Preda (ABC Cardinal) cites the Sala Constitucional's ruling on ex-senator Kattya González's expulsion, in which ministers Víctor Ríos and Gustavo Santander found due process violated, and says consistency would require a similar outcome; lawyer Manuel Riera (1000 AM) sees the action as exhausting domestic remedies en route to the IACHR; dissident Colorado Sen. Mario Varela (ÚH, 1000 Noticias) says it will not prosper. VOTE CONFLICT LARGELY RESOLVED: Varela, a sitting senator, states Diputados voted 78 of 78 present for the accusation and the Senate 44 of 44 present for removal — consistent with C-PEN-06 (44–0); ÚH's '43' is treated as an outlier. UPDATE v2.0: lawyer Cecilia Pérez argues the 17-page action omits his resignation and aims at the lifetime Senate seat (C-PEN-35).

claims.statement: EXPANDED IMPUTATION (Acta de Imputación N.º 11, causa penal N.º 92/2026 'Santiago Peña Palacios y otros s/ lesión de confianza y otros'), filed 24 Nov by prosecutors Christian M. Benítez Cáceres, Silvia González Vester, Elena Fiore Franco, Ruth Benítez, Laura Giacummo, Verónica Valdez Rivas and Marlene González (coordination: fiscal adjunta Nancy Salomón Marín), announced at an MP press conference minutes after the indagatorias of Francisco Peña and Rocío Caballero: (1) ex-President Santiago Peña Palacios — lavado de activos (coautor) and cohecho pasivo agravado (autor), added to lesión de confianza, administración en provecho propio and asociación criminal (Hoy: five offences in total); (2) his brother Francisco Peña Palacios — lavado de activos (coautor), cohecho pasivo agravado (cómplice), asociación criminal (autor), administración en provecho propio (cómplice); (3) Francisco's wife Rocío Caballero Bosch — lavado de activos (coautora). Requests: prisión preventiva for Francisco Peña (expected penalty up to 15 years), arresto domiciliario with ankle monitor for Caballero (up to 5 years), real precautionary measures (embargo-type) on both and on PEAR S.R.L., and a 6-month term for the conclusive act (pending: BCP, Superintendencia de Bancos and ueno-intervener reports, international legal cooperation). Prosecutors' hypothesis (MP note): PEAR S.R.L. (capital G. 6M) bought the 1,184-ha María Antonia (Paraguarí) property for US$3M from the then Financiera Ueno, financed by Financiera Ueno itself so the funds returned to the lender with no own contribution; instalments were paid not from PEAR's income but with transfers from Grupo Vázquez S.A.E. and ITTI S.A.E.C.A. accounts, backed by PEAR invoices for 'confección de granos forrajeros' for estancia Don Miguel; evidence includes deeds, beneficial-owner registry, DNIT records, invoices and statements supplied by ueno's interveners. ÚH/ABC summarise the theory as Peña promoting public placements in ueno and shielding it from control in exchange for the estancia and Luxembourg shares held in his brother's name. Further detail (Pulso Judicial, from the acta): the property had entered Financiera Ueno as dación en pago from Ueno Holding S.A.E.C.A. (where Peña held 6,144 shares); the mortgage line was for up to US$4,910,053.88; after 28 Feb 2024 Francisco held 99% and Rocío 1% of PEAR; Francisco entered U Holding S.à r.l. (Luxembourg) on 20 Mar 2024 (22 assignment contracts, 58 shares, US$58,000) and left it Mar–Apr 2025, in sync with the redemption of Peña's 6,144 Ueno Holding shares. CONFLICTS RECORDED: Rocío Caballero's offence — MP note, DW, ÚH, La Nación, 5Días: lavado de activos only; Agencia IP (state agency) and a search-indexed ABC version: cohecho pasivo agravado; LPO: lavado + administración en provecho propio. The MP note is treated as authoritative. Credit amount US$3M (price, MP) vs line up to US$4.91M (Pulso Judicial) — different measures, not reconciled. International: DW and Infobae (T3) confirm. All three are presumed innocent; no judicial ruling on the requested measures found at cut-off.

claims.statement: ALLEGATION — Fernández Valdovinos contract: on the Diputados floor (24 Nov) opposition deputy Rocío Vallejo (PPQ) read from a two-year 'consultoría estratégica' contract dated 6 Aug 2026 between Grupo Vázquez (signed by Miguel Vázquez as president, per ÚH) and ex-Economy Minister Carlos Fernández Valdovinos, to advise on the 'fusión y/o adquisición por parte de la sociedad de entidades financieras': fees US$20,000/month (VAT incl.), an extra US$60,000 in December and an annual bonus of 1% of the group bank's after-tax net profit. She recalls that as minister he decided on 28 Jul 2025 the placement of G. 250,000M of Caja Fiscal (pension) surpluses in ueno (+ G. 123,838M committed interest); he left the MEF on 31 Mar 2026 but remained on Itaipú's board (pay >G. 112M per ÚH vs G. 119M per Ñandutí — minor conflict) when he signed, and the contract came just over a year after the placement, so the one-year post-office restriction of Ley 2523 art. 4 (as amended Dec 2023) did not apply — 'se salvó por nueve días' (NPY, ABC). The contract was forwarded to the MP. Reactions: Sen. Gustavo Leite, ex-Sen. Désirée Masi and Central governor Ricardo Estigarribia demand prosecution action; LPO cites anonymous judicial sources saying imputations of Fernández Valdovinos and (ex-IPS head) Abreu are 'inminente' (unverified). Hoy prints the placement as 'G. 250.000.000' (apparent typo for G. 250,000M). Fernández Valdovinos' response NOT located; he was searched on 10 Nov (C-LEG-32) but is not imputed; presumed innocent. UPDATE v2.0 (25 Nov): ABC/ADN report Vallejo's documents (contract 6 Aug 2026, two-year term, 'consultoría estratégica' on mergers/partnerships of financial entities; he left the MEF on 31 Mar 2026); El Nacional values it at US$600,000 over two years plus bonuses; new allegation of a 2 Nov loan attempt by persons close to him (C-OTH-23); political demands for his imputation (C-OTH-24). Still no reply from him located; not imputed. UPDATE v2.1: ABC reports the document also mentions a performance bonus; Sen. Nakayama: if proven, 'gravísimo' (conflict of interest with his Itaipú board seat). Still NOT imputed (see C-OTH-28). UPDATE v2.4 (27 Nov): the contract is now described in an OFFICIAL MP note ordering his detention (C-LEG-46): dated 6 Aug 2026, signed personally while he was an Itaipú board member, two-year term, USD 20,000/month, USD 60,000 extra per year, 1% of annual net profit of a group financial entity — USD 600,000 fixed over two years (USD 1.2M if renewed). The MP treats it as a possible means of disguising payment tied to the 28 Jul 2025 Caja Fiscal authorisation (Res. MEF 338/2025) — a prosecutorial hypothesis, not a finding. Presumed innocent.

claims.statement: Precautionary-measure hearings (causa 92/2026) before Juez Penal de Garantías Especializado en Crimen Organizado Osmar Legal on 25 Nov: Francisco Peña Palacios (MP seeks prisión preventiva) at 09:00 PY and Rocío Caballero Bosch (MP seeks house arrest with ankle monitor) at 10:00 PY (ADN, ABC). Francisco Peña's lawyer Elías Gibbons said the defence still had no access to the expediente or the acta de imputación; Caballero's lawyer Federico Hetter said they had not seen the imputation either, rejected house arrest and argued she did not participate in the facts and the prosecution has not determined the object of the alleged laundering (Cuarto Poder, El Observador X). A journalist reported the hearing for Francisco Peña began at ~11:05 PY (14:05 UTC). NO RULING had been reported at the cut-off (~06:10 PT / 11:10 PY). Both remain presumed innocent. UPDATE (11:07 PY): El Observador posted that Francisco Peña and his lawyers were in judge Legal's office; it says prosecutors cite an expected sentence of up to 15 years in seeking prisión preventiva. RULING v2.1 (25 Nov afternoon PY): judge Osmar Legal ORDERED PRISIÓN PREVENTIVA for Francisco Peña Palacios, finding risk of flight and of obstruction, to be served at the Agrupación Especializada of the National Police (the defence had asked for alternative measures, arguing his closeness to the ex-President puts his life at risk in an ordinary prison — ÚH, Hoy). For Rocío Caballero Bosch he ordered HOUSE ARREST WITHOUT ankle monitor (A.I. N.º 428 per 1000 Noticias/Cuarto Poder), under random police checks, with bans on leaving the country, changing address or phone, and contacting co-defendants; he accepted a fianza real of G. 13,000M via executive attachment of two properties (Ñandutí, ÚH, ABC; Cuarto Poder reports G. 13,284M — figure discrepancy). She abstained from testifying. For both, a general inhibition to sell or encumber present and future assets, and requests to the Superintendencia de Bancos and INCOOP for accounts, CDAs and investments (El Nacional, ADN, Hoy). The MP has until 25 May 2027 for its conclusive request (Ñandutí). Both remain presumed innocent. UPDATE v2.2: per ABC, judge Legal also ordered preventive attachment (embargo preventivo), a prohibition to innovate and to contract over the PEAR S.R.L. rural property in María Antonia district, oficios to the Registros Públicos, the vehicle registry, the Superintendencia de Bancos, Incoop and Senacsa, and information on both spouses' bank accounts, deposits and investments; Francisco Peña was taken to the Agrupación Especializada on 25 Nov afternoon (C9N; police chief described visiting rules). Both presumed innocent.

claims.statement: Itaipú exposure — NEW FIGURE from its Paraguayan director-general Hugo Zárate (Ñandutí 'La Gran Cabina' interview, 25 Nov, via Ñandutí X posts): at the time ueno closed Itaipú held ~US$183M in dollar and guaraní accounts, plus ~US$42M in accounts of the Parque Tecnológico Itaipú (PTI) used to fund agreements with Itaipú and ministries — together ~US$228M as he put it (note: 183 + 42 = 225; the rounded total is his). Fundación Tesãi had no deposits; Cajubi funds are a separate case. He said the 2024/Jan 2025 Executive Board resolution only updated the list of authorised banks and did not order deposits (operations are the Finance Directorate's remit); 'No puedo decir que se nos ocultó nada' on ueno's ratings — ex-board member Pedro Ferreira disputed this. He confirmed an ANDE payment of ~US$40M to Itaipú's account in September but could not say how much went into ueno; he has requested a full movement report since the accounts opened (Jan 2025); the funds are 'solamente paraguayos' and possible complaints are being evaluated. CONFLICT with earlier figures: US$163.8M + G. 115,200M at 3 Nov (Itaipú communiqué via ADN/El Independiente), ~US$181–182M (La Nación), >US$200M (board member Duarte Frutos). UPDATE v2.2 (25 Nov evening): Itaipú board members Nicanor Duarte Frutos and Marco Riquelme (also Industry minister) put Itaipú + PTI funds in ueno at US$220–222M, all from the Paraguayan side, contrary to the distinction drawn by FM Ramírez Lezcano (ABC) — a FIFTH figure, recorded alongside the others. Zárate (ABC, Ñandutí) said the board's Res. RDE-004/2025 of 15 Jan 2025, which he signed, added ueno as the 9th authorised bank with a favourable opinion; the five-years-in-market rule was not put to the board (it is used only by the Financial Directorate); the resolution did not order deposits; he will show documents only to the courts. SNT reports, on 'preliminary information' and without a named source, that Itaipú tripled its ueno deposits in the two weeks before the collapse (unverified). UPDATE v2.3 (26 Nov): Foreign Minister Ramírez, speaking to Brazil's foreign minister, pledged to restore Itaipú funds, both 'soberanos' and those of the binational; he gave no amount or method. Presidency sources told ABC the amounts are US$ 163.8 million and G. 115,200 million (the 7 Nov Itaipú communiqué: US$ 163.8M plus guaraníes totalling about US$ 182M). Itaipú interim DG Hugo Zárate (Monumental AM, via ÚH; also Hoy) itemised about USD 163 million (Hoy: US$ 163.8M) in the dollar account and G. 115,000 million (Hoy: G. 115,200 million) in the guaraní account at the close, plus PTI project accounts of about US$ 40 million in nine accounts (Hoy) / 'varios' accounts (ÚH), for a combined figure of about US$ 220 million (ÚH) or about US$ 183M + ~US$ 40M PTI (Hoy). This tends to RECONCILE the earlier US$ 220–222M board-member figure as Itaipú + PTI, not a fifth independent Itaipú-only total. ÚH reports works delayed and no fully defined plan; Zárate also said Itaipú can meet obligations (incl. ANDE transfers) from funds in other banks, would 'contingenciar' retained sums, and that Itaipú has filed a criminal complaint against the bank and its directors over retained Itaipú and PTI funds. He is not a criminal defendant in that complaint's target list as reported. Alliana's restitution pledge still has no published funding source. UPDATE v2.4 (27 Nov): Zárate (Medios del Estado via El Nacional) restated ~USD 183M retained (G. 115,200M + USD 163.8M) plus ~USD 40M in nine PTI accounts — nine of 81 PTI agreements are affected, incl. projects with MITIC, MOPC and INCAN; obligations incl. monthly ANDE transfers covered; alternatives being studied for the affected projects. Ex-Itaipú director Balmelli alleged a 'political order' to deposit (~USD 200M) in the final weeks and that Brazilian directors also approved (C-OTH-35) — allegation only.

claims.statement: Workers' advance bill FILED (follow-up to C-PUB-20/C-PUB-22): on 25 Nov President Pedro Alliana sent Congress, with a request for URGENT treatment, a bill creating an exceptional regime of advances on labour credits for workers of companies linked to the ueno bank economic group that ceased operations after the BCP resolution. Per the text as reported: >4,000 workers of about 40 companies; each may receive an amount equal to their certified credits up to a uniform cap of FIVE MONTHLY MINIMUM WAGES (just over G. 15M), covering unpaid wages, severance, proportional aguinaldo and holidays, and notice; fund of up to G. 62,000M via 2026 budget modifications by the MEF, held in a special account; voluntary, individual, free (no lawyers/intermediaries), application within 60 calendar days in person or online; it is an advance, not a subsidy — workers keep the right to claim the balance from the employer; the State subrogates and recovers from employers or from confiscated assets in the criminal cases; sums are unattachable (except child support); IPS health cover extended to 31 Dec 2026; directors, managers, attorneys-in-fact, shareholders and close relatives are excluded; joining implies formal termination of the labour relationship (Hoy). Labour Minister Mónica Recalde (C9N): ~4,000 workers, up to G. 15M each, the State has priority to recover. FIGURE CONTEXT: the bill's >4,000 workers / ~40 firms differs from the 3,610 workers in 22 firms cited earlier by the ministry and ÚH (C-PUB-22) — different scope, recorded side by side. UPDATE v2.3 (26 Nov): Senate president Basilio Núñez said the bill will not be taken this week (the 2027 budget comes first) and is expected next week after committee reports; he said ueno-related items would have 'prioridad'. Ex-workers marched again to demand 100% of severance, not only the five-minimum-wage (~G. 15,220,000) advance; they say they will file collective claims for the balance (ÚH). RDN describes the delayed aid as for 4,000 workers. Still not voted. UPDATE v2.4 (La Tribuna, 27 Nov): workers marched to Congress on Thu 26 Nov demanding full severance and a mechanism to collect the balance after the advance; they submitted proposed amendments; the Senate is expected to take the bill next week.

claims.statement: Special-law bill (26 Nov): Schreiner said the BCP has sent the Executive, with a request for urgent treatment, a draft to create an intermediate EXTRAJUDICIAL LIQUIDATION stage not now in the deposit-guarantee law — compensations, dación en pago and agreements with non-depositor creditors (incl. local and international bondholders) before a judicial bankruptcy. The BCP board would appoint a liquidator for up to 180 days, extendable by six months, with civil and penal responsibility and accounts. The scheme was agreed with the bankers' association and replaces an earlier, slower trust idea. UPDATE v2.4 (ABC, 27 Nov): ABC again reports the bill as sent by the BCP to the head of the Executive with an urgency request (supporting the 'Executive, not yet Congress' version). Its working title: modification and extension of the deposit-guarantee and bank-resolution law plus extraordinary measures in ueno's resolution; it would change the FGD least-cost calculation, create a special asset-administration stage before judicial liquidation, and add ueno-specific rules on confiscated assets; local and international bondholders could receive parts of the loan book. claims.statement: International asset tracing (26 Nov). claims.statement: DETENTION ORDER — ex-Minister of Economy and Finance Carlos Gustavo Fernández Valdovinos (Fri 27 Nov). Official MP note: prosecutors Christian M. Benítez Cáceres, Silvia Margarita González Vester, Elena Fiore, Laura Giacummo, Ruth Benítez and Marlene González (Unidad Especializada de Delitos Económicos y Anticorrupción) ordered his detention for the alleged offences of administración en provecho propio, cohecho pasivo agravado, asociación criminal and lavado de activos; the order was sent to the Police Commander by Oficio N.º 327 under art. 240 CPP, and the team wants him to give a declaración indagatoria. Prosecutors' account of the facts (allegations): on 28 Jul 2025, as minister, he signed Resolución M.E.F. N.º 338/2025 authorising the placement of G. 250,000 million of Caja Fiscal pension funds in five-year ueno bank CDAs; on 6 Aug 2026, after leaving the ministry and while a member of Itaipú's board, he personally signed a 'consultoría estratégica' contract with Grupo Vázquez S.A.E. — two years, USD 20,000/month, an extra USD 60,000 a year and a bonus of 1% of the annual net profit of a group financial entity — a fixed USD 600,000 over two years (up to USD 1.2 million if renewed), which the MP hypothesises was a way to give a legal appearance to pay linked to the 28 Jul 2025 authorisation. The MP also investigates his alleged part in an organised structure of Executive and regulator officials that favoured the group. La Nación and El Nacional place the order in causa penal N.º 92/2026 (Peña, Carvallo, Insfrán, González, Caballero, Mora and others); El Nacional cites 'Resolución Fiscal de Detención N.º 13' of 27 Nov. ADN also describes him as an ex-BCP president; ABC's wording that the suspicions concern his time 'al frente del BCP' is not reflected in the MP note (which concerns his MEF and post-MEF acts) — wording discrepancy recorded. STATUS AT CUT-OFF (~06:30 PT / 11:30 PY): police were guarding his home; Asunción police chief Francisco Ávalos said they were not certain he was inside and awaited a search warrant (Ñandutí, El Observador). He had NOT been reported detained, and he is NOT reported as imputed (a detention order is not an imputation). One unverified X account claimed he is a fugitive — NOT confirmed by any PY outlet or official source. His reply was not located. Presumed innocent.
